title: Thirty-Second Developer Signal: pricing & quickstart messaging
content:
Purpose:
Small, skimmable brief for copywriters and product marketers to use when writing landing pages, SDK docs, and first-email flows. The concept: a 30-second "developer signal" — a piece of copy and a quickstart that proves value (latency, cost clarity, and time-to-first-call) in under 30s.

TL;DR:
- Build messaging that leads with "30s to your first inference" and an explicit economic line ("pay-per-token, clear cost estimator") so engineers can judge viability without sales.
- Provide three quickstart paths (30s hello, 5m embed, 1-day prod stub) with exact code snippets and expected latency/cost numbers.
- Pricing language must clearly state unit economics and optional reserved capacity for predictable throughput.

Developer-first value props (candidate headlines & supporting bullets):
1) "Get a result in 30s — integrate in minutes": emphasize SDK samples, single-line curl, and streaming responses. Include expected p95 latency for common models (e.g., 200–400ms for short prompts on curated small models).
2) "Understand cost before you ship": show a token estimator inline, default model cost labels, and a short note: "pay-as-you-go or reserve capacity for 20–40% savings at scale."
3) "Same API for hosted, dedicated, and private": show a single config snippet that toggles deployment mode to underline portability.
4) "Production controls, not just models": highlight rollouts, fallbacks, and per-route observability as developer controls (A/B, canary).

Quickstart angles (copy + brief dev flow):
A) Thirty-Second Hello (target: evaluate in <30s)
  - Copy: "Paste this curl. See text in seconds. No keys, no config." (offer ephemeral demo token on the page)
  - Snippet: single curl that returns a short completion + streaming prompt sample.
  - Expectations to put next to snippet: "Median response: ~350ms. Typical cost: $0.002 per 100 tokens (small model)."

B) Five-Minute Embed (target: prototype in 5 minutes)
  - Copy: "Add LLM search, chat, or summarization with three lines of code and our JS SDK."
  - Steps: install SDK, init with apiKey, call /generate with short prompt, enable streaming.
  - Outcome: measurable delta (character count, tokens) and one chart: p50/p95 latency from console.

C) One-Day Stub-to-Prod (target: working prod path in 24 hours)
  - Copy: "From prototype to rollout — use model pinning, canary, and autoscale policies."
  - Steps: pin a model, deploy route, set a canary (10% traffic), enable fallback route.
  - Economic note: show how batching & KV cache reduce token spend by X% depending on workload (placeholder numbers with CTA to Optimize).

Pricing-language drafts (snippets for web and emails):
- Hero line: "Simple, predictable pricing — pay per token or reserve capacity for predictable throughput."
- Short blurb: "Free trial credits, then pay-as-you-go with transparent per‑token rates. Reserve Dedicated pools for committed throughput and discounted unit costs."
- FAQ microcopy: "How much will this cost? Use the in-console estimator (tokens × model price) — or try the calculator for projected monthly spend at your expected RPS."
- Pricing tiers to present: Free credits (onboarding), Pay-as-you-go (hosted; per-token), Developer bundle (metered monthly with small credit), Reserved/Dedicated (commit discounts + SLA), Private (license + infra fee).
- Suggested copy for reserved discounts: "Commit to a monthly throughput and save 20–40% on units; exact savings depend on model mix and batching."

Competitive analysis notes (quick bulleted comparisons to use in pitch-sidecards):
- OpenAI: strong brand & model breadth; weaker on dedicated/private deployment and transparent unit-cost tooling. Position: "Similar developer experience, more production controls and clearer economics."
- Anthropic: safety-first messaging and chat models; emphasize Redwood's deployment choice (private) + routing/fallback controls as advantage.
- Cloud vendors (AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex): enterprise integration and cloud bundling; call out Redwood's lower friction to integrate and runtime optimizations focused on latency/cost for standard LLM workloads.
- Self-host/inference vendors: more control but higher ops cost; highlight Redwood's unified API across hosted/dedicated/private so teams don't rework app logic.

Metrics to surface on pages & quickstarts (conservative phrasing):
- Typical first-call latency: 300–800ms (depends on model & prompt).
- Sample unit cost: $0.001–$0.01 per 1k tokens depending on model size and quantization.
- Committed discount range: 20–40% off hosted per-token equivalent for reserved Dedicated.

Objections & short rebuttals for sales/evangelists:
- "We run on top of cloud GPUs already." -> "Redwood reduces per-token unit cost through batching, KV caching, and routing — often lower total cost and less engineering time than building the same runtime yourself."
- "I need private/VPC only." -> "Private deployment offers the same API and rollout tooling with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integrations."
- "Pricing is too fuzzy." -> "Add the estimator next to every sample and show a worked example: 1k requests/day × avg 200 tokens = $X/month."

Microcopy and UX recommendations for the onramp flow:
- Entry CTA: "Try a 30s demo — no credit card."
- Inline unit tags: for each model in the picker show a small tag: "~$0.002 / 1k tokens · 300ms p50".
- In emails: subject lines to A/B test: "30s to your first inference" vs "Estimate your model costs in 60s"

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Need validated latency & unit cost benchmarks for 3 curated models (small, medium, chat) to replace placeholders. Action: eng-applied-ml to run standard prompt suite and return p50/p95 + cost.
- Create a demo token flow that generates ephemeral keys for the 30s demo (security/abuse guardrails needed).
- Legal review for pricing language around committed discounts and SLA language.

Notes to writer: keep copy lean, technical, and confidence-first. Avoid vague promises like "cheapest"; prefer measurable statements and call-to-actions that invite experimentation (e.g., "Run this curl in 30s").

Rough next steps:
1) Get latency/cost numbers from applied-ml (ENG-5123).
2) Wire up a page with the three quickstart flows and an inline estimator (PR #78).
3) Draft price page microcopy and hand to pricing for compliance review.

Document history: created as workshop output for Q4 GTM sprint. This is a working draft — expect edits to the metrics and pricing copy once benchmarks land.
